candidate.blueprint_locator: Client Needs category 'Psychosocial Integrity' — nursing care that promotes and supports emotional, mental and social well-being; applied here to family/caregiver coping, support systems, stress management, therapeutic assessment and resource referral.
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize significant caregiver burden when caregiving demands exceed available resources and respond by assessing caregiver capacity and connecting the family with individualized practical, respite, and psychosocial support.

options.A: Assess the caregiver's current demands, available resources, and ability to perform care safely, then help identify support that matches the needs, such as sharing tasks, respite care, or social-work/counseling resources.
options.B: Encourage the spouse to continue all caregiving duties alone because accepting outside help generally increases caregiver burden.
options.C: Reassure the spouse that severe exhaustion is an expected part of caregiving and needs no intervention unless the client is hospitalized.
options.D: Focus only on the client's symptoms because caregiver sleep loss, work strain, and concerns about managing medications are unrelated to safe home care.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. NCI defines caregiver burden as stress or strain that occurs when caregiving demands exceed the resources available to the caregiver. Cancer caregivers can have emotional, social, financial, work-related, and health needs, and NCI emphasizes recognizing caregiver roles and challenges, asking what help is needed, sharing tasks, seeking support, and using respite or professional resources when appropriate. In this scenario, severe sleep loss plus concern about medication mistakes makes an assessment of caregiving capacity and available support clinically important. B is incorrect because NCI encourages caregivers to accept help and share responsibilities rather than assuming they must do everything alone. C inappropriately normalizes potentially unsafe exhaustion. D is incorrect because NCI treats caregiver well-being and ability to perform caregiving tasks as relevant to cancer care.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Caregiver burden occurs when caregiving demands exceed available resources; cancer caregivers may experience emotional, social, financial, employment, and health strain; clinicians should recognize caregiver needs and support task-sharing, respite, counseling/social-work, and other resources as appropriate.
